title: Morgan Stanley: AI Investment's True Scale Underestimated—2027 Capex Could Reach $1.58 Trillion When Leases Are Included
key_facts: Morgan Stanley (Nicholas Lentini's team) estimates total AI compute investment including leases at about $980 billion in 2026, $1.58 trillion in 2027 and $1.81 trillion in 2028.
The 2027 figure is about 14% above the traditional cash capital-spending measure, because data-centre leases do not appear in capex or in management guidance.
Hyperscalers have disclosed more than $1.1 trillion of lease commitments that have not yet started.

Morgan Stanley expects 2027 to be the year with the largest cash flow deficit in its forecast period; hyperscalers have issued about $255 billion of unsecured bonds this year, and 10-year all-in yields are up about 100 to 180 basis points since the end of 2025.

Highly rated borrowers (Amazon, Meta, Google, Microsoft) have interest cover of about 30.7 times; lower-rated ones such as Oracle about 4 times, falling to about 1.8 times if they borrow another $120 billion in 2027.
The bank estimates returns on new compute capacity at 25% to 50%, and says about 65% of AI capex ends up in S&P 500 companies' revenue, with Nvidia taking about two-thirds of that.
quote_evidence: Morgan Stanley's latest research shows that when lease financing is included, total AI compute investment by hyperscalers and emerging cloud providers will reach approximately $1.58 trillion in 2027—about 14% larger than the traditional cash capex measure.
Data center leases are economically equivalent to debt-financed asset purchases, but they do not appear as capital expenditures on cash flow statements, nor do they enter management's capex guidance.
Morgan Stanley estimates that 2027 will be the largest cash flow deficit year in its forecast period.
why_it_matters_hint: The real size of AI spending, and of the debt behind it, is larger than company capex figures show.
event_date: Research note reported 16 Oct 2026; note date not stated
notes: BigGo Finance is an aggregator; the Morgan Stanley note itself was not seen. The article says the increase from 2026 to 2027 is about $700 billion, but its own figures ($980 billion to $1.58 trillion) imply about $600 billion, so that figure is not used. The same article also covers a separate JPMorgan note (Google Cloud, AWS, Meta, Fiverr), not used here.
